name: Donoghue v Stevenson
principle: A person owes a duty to take reasonable care to avoid acts or omissions that could reasonably be foreseen to injure their 'neighbour'.
summary: A manufacturer owed a duty of care to the ultimate consumer of a bottled drink containing a decomposed snail.

name: Overseas Tankship (UK) Ltd v Morts Dock (The Wagon Mound No 1)
court: Privy Council (on appeal from New South Wales)
principle: A defendant is liable in negligence only for damage of a kind that was reasonably foreseeable.
summary: Oil spilled in Sydney Harbour later ignited; the fire damage was held too remote because it was not reasonably foreseeable.

name: Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co
principle: An advertisement can be a unilateral offer to the world, accepted by performing its conditions.
summary: A company that advertised a reward and deposited money to show sincerity was bound to pay a user who caught influenza.

name: Hadley v Baxendale
principle: Damages for breach of contract cover losses arising naturally from the breach or reasonably in the contemplation of both parties when contracting.
summary: A carrier delayed delivering a broken mill shaft; the mill owner's lost profits were too remote to recover.

name: Salomon v A Salomon & Co Ltd
principle: A properly incorporated company is a legal person separate from its shareholders, who are not liable for its debts.
summary: Mr Salomon was not personally liable for the debts of his one-man company, which had been validly incorporated.

name: Rylands v Fletcher
principle: A person who brings onto land and keeps there something likely to do mischief if it escapes is answerable for the damage caused by its escape.
summary: Water from a reservoir flooded a neighbour's mine; the landowner was liable although he was not negligent.

name: Ukeje v Ukeje
citation: Supreme Court of Nigeria (2014); confirm the law report citation
principle: A customary law denying a female child a share in her late father's estate is discriminatory and unconstitutional.
summary: The Supreme Court held that Igbo customary law excluding daughters from inheritance conflicts with the constitutional right to freedom from discrimination.

name: Mojekwu v Mojekwu
principle: A custom that is discriminatory and contrary to natural justice, equity and good conscience will not be enforced.
summary: The Court of Appeal refused to enforce the Nnewi oli-ekpe custom that deprived a woman of rights in her late husband's estate.
